edits.old: Compare the same query with and without a hint using explain("executionStats"). Inspect the selected index and scan work, documents examined, elapsed time, bucket unpacking, and sort stages before retaining the hint; selecting an index alone is insufficient evidence of improvement. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Use explain("executionStats") to check whether a time series query uses the intended index, and compare it with the same query run without a hint. Look at the documents and index keys examined (totalDocsExamined, totalKeysExamined). Treat executionTimeMillis with caution: it is not necessarily representative of actual query time, and a hinted explain bypasses plan selection and can report a lower time. Do not rely on index selection alone as evidence of improvement. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md

edits.rationale: MongoDB documents explain("executionStats") as the way to confirm secondary-index use on time series collections. It defines totalDocsExamined and totalKeysExamined, and it warns that executionTimeMillis can be misleading when cursor.hint() is used with explain. No MongoDB page prescribes the full hinted-versus-unhinted workflow, and none names bucket-unpacking or sort stages as checks, so those parts are the pack's own advice. The claim is therefore kept only in the scope the sources support.
